title: Wing and Walmart are bringing drone deliveries to Denver and Seattle in 2027
key_facts: Walmart and Alphabet-owned Wing have revealed two more metro areas for their drone delivery service, Denver and Seattle, with operations planned to start in 2027.
It is part of a plan to offer air delivery from more than 270 Walmart stores across the US, which the companies 'eventually' plan to do.
Drone deliveries are currently available in five metro areas: Atlanta; Charlotte, North Carolina; Dallas-Fort Worth; Houston; and Orlando, Florida.

Engadget says the companies aim to expand to fourteen other destinations, including Miami, Philadelphia, Los Angeles and the San Francisco Bay Area; it does not say whether Denver and Seattle are among the fourteen.
The drones can travel at up to 60 mph and carry a payload of up to five pounds.
If a Walmart order is eligible for drone delivery, customers see it as an option on the Walmart app or website; consumers can also order through Wing's own app.
The announcement came days after DoorDash gave more details of its own drone service, DoorDash Air, which will debut in northern California with partners including Chipotle and Popeyes.
quote_evidence: The companies plan to start operations in the Denver and Seattle metro areas in 2027 as part of a plan to offer air delivery from more than 270 Walmart stores across the US.
Currently, Wing and Walmart's drone deliveries are available in five metropolitan areas: Atlanta; Charlotte, North Carolina; Dallas–Fort Worth; Houston; and Orlando, Florida.
The drones can travel at up to 60 mph and carry a payload that weighs as much as five pounds.
why_it_matters_hint: Drone delivery from a major US retailer is already running in five metro areas and is planned to spread to more than 270 stores, so shoppers in more cities are set to get it, though only for eligible, light orders.
event_date: Announced about 5 Oct 2026; the Denver and Seattle start is planned for 2027.
notes: Read in full; the Engadget text is short (about 1,100 characters) and names no outside source, so Engadget is credited; status REPORTED because it relays the companies' announcement without quoting either of them. These are announced plans with no store counts or city-by-city dates. The five current metro areas are operating today; the new part is the 2027 plan for Denver and Seattle.
